facts: $d = \sqrt{(x_2 - x_1)^2 + (y_2 - y_1)^2}$ — the run is $x_2 - x_1$ and the rise is $y_2 - y_1$.
Squaring removes the signs, so it does not matter which point is $(x_1, y_1)$.
Leave a non-whole answer as an exact surd in simplest form, such as $2\sqrt{5}$, or round as the question asks.
A horizontal interval has distance $|x_2-x_1|$ and a vertical interval has distance $|y_2-y_1|$, since distance cannot be negative.
steps: Label the coordinates $(x_1, y_1)$ and $(x_2, y_2)$.
Square each bracket, add, then take the square root last, giving an exact or rounded answer as required.

workedExamples.question_text: Find the distance between $P(-4,6)$ and $Q(2,0)$. Give your answer in simplest surd form and correct to $2$ decimal places.
The distance between $A(-1,2)$ and $B(3,k)$ is $\sqrt{41}$ units. Find the two possible values of $k$.
Which of the points $A(-2,0)$, $B(5,3)$ and $C(1,-2)$ is closest to $D(1,2)$?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}DA&=\sqrt{(-2-1)^2+(0-2)^2}\\&=\sqrt{9+4}\\&=\sqrt{13}\text{ units}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}DB&=\sqrt{(5-1)^2+(3-2)^2}\\&=\sqrt{16+1}\\&=\sqrt{17}\text{ units}\end{aligned}$

$\begin{aligned}DC&=\sqrt{(1-1)^2+(-2-2)^2}\\&=\sqrt{16}\\&=4\text{ units}\end{aligned}$

Since $\sqrt{13}<4<\sqrt{17}$, point $A$ is closest to $D$.
